key_insight: The paper reports strong evidence for a stable finite-time singularity in the 3D Euler equations on \(\mathbb{R}^3\), supported by a self-similar profile at the critical blowup rate of 0.5.
engineering_relevance: This suggests AI-assisted symbolic-numerical pipelines can help formulate and certify extreme-flow hypotheses that are otherwise difficult to analyze analytically.
method: Used a physics-informed neural network (PINN) with a self-similar ansatz to learn an approximate blowup profile.
Certified the learned profile with a spline representation for rigorous downstream analysis.
Analyzed the associated transport field to assess damping and nonlinear stability conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites an approximate singular profile, spline-based certification, and a stability framework reduced to finite explicit estimates and computable constants.
watch_item: The result is evidence-based rather than a complete proof of singularity/stability, so the certification depends on the quality of the approximation and the remaining explicit estimates.
paper_title: Stable Singularity of the Euler Equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$
